title: review-gate trusted any PR comment as a sign-off

expected.text: Only team sign-offs should count toward review-gate before a PR can merge.

actual.text: Shield blocked PR #5. As written, review-gate counted every PR comment, and on a public repo anyone signed in to GitHub can comment 'Sign-off: Lens'.

why.text: The gate matched the comment text but never checked who wrote it. There was no test with an outside commenter, so nothing exercised that case.

change.text: check.py trusted() counts only comments whose author is OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR, with a test. It shipped in the same PR before merge, so the Block was right.

title: Research notes would not have rendered: build.py read old fields

expected.text: build.py renders every research note in the standard report format the research pipeline set up.

actual.text: The first real report made the build fail. build.py still read the old fields (topic, takeaways, sources), so no research note could render.

why.text: While data/research.json was empty, no test rendered a real note, so the stale field names never ran.

change.text: #22 renders the standard report and adds a test that builds the Team chat page from real research data (tests/test_decisions.py).

title: The published stylesheet had a badge at 3.5:1 in dark mode

expected.text: All text on the site meets 4.5:1 contrast in both themes.

actual.text: On its first run, the new contrast test found the published red 'no/vetoed' badge style at 3.5:1 in dark mode, under the 4.5:1 rule.

why.text: Theme colors were only checked by hand, so nothing stopped a later color from failing (backlog d4).

change.text: tests/test_contrast.py checks every theme text color for 4.5:1 in CI and bans hard-coded colors. The badge became a --bad theme variable (7.5:1 in dark).

title: Twice, a bot/data-* PR carried files the branch type doesn't allow

expected.text: Each PR uses the branch type that fits its paths. bot/data-* PRs touch only data/ and site/.

actual.text: The bot/data-* path rule failed twice: first on scripts/build.py and tests/test_decisions.py in the PR that #22 replaced, then on plans/direction.md in #35.

why.text: The branch type was picked from the main task (data) before all the changed paths were known. CI was right both times. The fixes were a bot/ops-* branch (#22) and a separate plan PR (#36).

change.text: Advisor rule in bots/forge.md: choose the branch type after listing the changed paths. Code or plan changes get their own bot/feature-*, bot/ops-*, or plan PR.

title: Two PRs hit review-gate missing a required sign-off

expected.text: Every role that the changed paths require signs off before a PR is marked ready.

actual.text: review-gate failed on #38 (missing Coordinator, for docs/design screenshots) and on #42 (missing Trial, for site/ changes). Each was fixed with the missing sign-off and a re-run.

why.text: Sign-offs were chosen from memory instead of from classify() in check.py, so less obvious paths were missed.

change.text: Forge rule (#46): list the required roles from classify() for the changed paths, and get each sign-off before gh pr ready.

title: Team chat c79 to c82 were published with times later than the work happened

expected.text: Each chat time is the real time the message was written.

actual.text: c79 to c82 went out in #42 with times 08:05 to 08:12 ET, but #42 merged at 07:36 ET. #44 corrected them to 07:34 to 07:36 ET.

why.text: The times were estimated ahead of the work instead of read from the clock, and no check compared a chat time with the time it was published.

change.text: Forge rule (#46): chat times come from the clock. #49 adds a CI check that fails on any chat time later than the time CI runs.

title: Team chat page reached 99.9% of its page-weight budget

expected.text: Each page stays inside the 100 KB page-weight budget, with room for the next run.

actual.text: The daily run found Team chat at 102,253 of 102,400 bytes. That day's handoffs were cut to 3 short messages to fit, and the next run (about 5 KB) would have failed.

why.text: The page rendered every thread ever posted, so it grew with every run and nothing rolled old items off.

change.text: #48 rolls older items to dated archive pages and keeps the main page near 50%. A test fails if it reaches 60%, and every link must still resolve.

title: A sign-off on #53 stated the wrong sitemap page count

expected.text: Every number in a sign-off matches the artifact it describes.

actual.text: Trial's sign-off on #53 said sitemap.xml lists all 26 HTML pages. It lists 15. The comment was corrected the same run, with a note.

why.text: The number came from the build summary ('built 26 files', which counts every generated file), not from counting the sitemap's entries.

change.text: Trial rule in bots/trial.md: counts in a sign-off come from a command run against the file itself. CI already checks that the sitemap lists every page (#54).

title: Team page win dates used UTC, a day late for 15 merged PRs

expected.text: Every date on the site is in ET, the zone the team and Ryno work in.

actual.text: 15 of the 48 wins in data/wins.json (#5, #6, #16 to #20, #22 to #29) carried the UTC date of their merge, one day after the ET date. For example, #29 merged at 23:20 ET on Oct 16 but showed Oct 17.

why.text: scripts/wins.py cut the date from GitHub's UTC timestamp (mergedAt[:10]) without converting it to ET, and no test compared a win's date with its merge time.

change.text: wins.py converts each merge time to ET and stores it as merged. A new test fails if any win's date isn't the ET date of its merge. The Timeline uses the same ET times.

title: Timeline put #65 and #66 under the wrong decision for about 10 minutes

expected.text: Each merged PR on the Timeline sits under the sprint or decision that shipped it, and nowhere else.

actual.text: From #67 (merged 18:10 ET) until this fix, the live Timeline listed #65 and #66 under i32, the Timeline page decision, instead of the Game Master sprint (i35).

why.text: #64 marked i32 shipped. The Timeline treated any shipped CEO decision with no retro range as a running sprint, so it took every PR merged after 5:26 PM ET. No test checked which PRs a decision groups.

change.text: A shipped decision that isn't a cap override now groups only the PRs its shipped field names. A new test fails if a decision groups any other PR, or if a PR sits in two groups.

title: /work/ hub titles broke letter by letter on phones; four sign-offs given without looking

expected.text: On a 390px phone, every hub card title sits on its own full-width line and no text runs past the screen edge. Design sign-offs come from people who looked at the pages.

actual.text: From #74 (merged 19:30 ET) to #77 (live 20:24 ET), /work/, Under the hood and the home stats rendered titles one or two letters per line ('Ti/m/eli/ne'). Ryno found it from his phone. #72 to #76 were signed off on audit numbers alone.

why.text: A tap-target rule in #74 (main li>a:only-child as inline-flex) made each hub link a side-by-side flex row. The audit checked only page width and tap size, not words split mid-word, overflow inside a box, or clipped text. Nobody looked at the pages, and Critic said it was fine in c224.

change.text: #77 fixed every page and added 4 visual checks (mid-word, narrow column, in-box overflow, past the right edge, clipped included); they fail on the old CSS. #78 makes bot.py refuse a design or CSS PR without screenshots of every page and Polish and Trial sign-offs naming what they reviewed.

title: 6 shipped ideas still showed as approved, not built

expected.text: When an approved idea's PRs merge, its record says shipped and links them, so the tracker's open ideas are real open work.

actual.text: i9, i21, i28, i29, i33 and i36 shipped in #22 to #29, #35 to #44, #52, #53, #65 and #70 to #76 (Oct 16 and 17) but stayed 'yes' until today. Game Master flagged stale yes ideas in c295; Lens counted them in c306.

why.text: Sprints shipped under their own sprint ideas (i16, i24, i35, i37), and only those were closed at retro. Nothing tied the original pitch to the merged PRs, and no check looked for an approved idea that merged PRs had already named.

change.text: #94 closes the 6 with their PRs. New add-only test: an approved idea named in a merged PR title must be backed by an open objective in data/objectives.json, or CI fails. i34 stays open, tied to Game Master's Week 2 objective.

title: The tempo records in c310 split failed PR runs wrongly (15 and 16, not 18 and 13)

expected.text: Every number in a team record is derived from its source, splits included, and checked the same way before merge.

actual.text: c310, merged in #92, said 15 failed bot PR runs and 16 on Dependabot. GitHub's run list gives 18 bot and 13 Dependabot (31 total, which was right). Lens's #92 sign-off repeated the wrong split. Both were live on the site for about 30 minutes.

why.text: Analyst counted the split by eye from a printed list instead of computing it, and Lens re-derived the total but not the split.

change.text: #96 corrects c310. Lens now re-derives every split, not just totals (c318). Advisor's tempo tripwire proposal (c321, c322) counts AARs like this one in code.

title: A #98 sign-off said 91 main runs, not 92, and every #98 sign-off was posted twice

expected.text: Each sign-off is posted once, and every count in it matches its record.

actual.text: Lens's first #98 sign-off said '90 CI and 90 Pages runs plus #97'. data/ci.json has 92 of each. The corrected text was posted too, so #98 has each of its 3 sign-offs twice, and the wrong one is still on the PR.

why.text: Lens added up the runs from memory instead of reading data/ci.json. Forge thought the first bot.py run had died, but it was waiting for review shots. The resume posted a second set of sign-offs.

change.text: #99 records the correction. Sign-offs quote counts only after reading them from the file at sign-off time (Lens, c339). Before any resume, Forge confirms the run has stopped and reads the PR's comments (c338). This AAR trips the pace again.

title: #108's guardrail gate read the new word-limits file as a loosening and labeled it needs-ceo

expected.text: Creating data/word_limits.json and data/voice.json only adds limits, so the guardrail gate passes.

actual.text: guardrail-gate failed on #108: 'loosens a guardrail: data/word_limits.json', and CI added the needs-ceo label.

why.text: words_loosened() treats any new exempt key as an added exemption. In a new file every key is new, and no test covered creating the file.

change.text: A new file (no removed lines, an opening brace added) is not loosening; a test covers creating both files and still flags a new exemption.
